articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic end losing skid and take top spot back from Rangers
articles.summary: Bhoys on top of table, while Rangers beat Kilmarnock 3-1. Calvin Miller scores two penalties in Hearts 5-0 St Mirren. Jota made his long-awaited return to action as Celtic claimed a much-needed 2-0 victory at Motherwell to move top of the Premiership again and ease the sense of gloom and tension…
body: Five months on from a dramatic late win that helped them on their way to last season’s title, Martin O’Neill’s side enjoyed another big result at Fir Park to end a three-game losing streak and climb back ahead of Rangers, who had leapfrogged them at the summit on Saturday.

After a renewal of hostilities between supporters and the Celtic board as well as uncertainty about O’Neill’s future as manager during the three-week break since their home defeat by their bitter rivals, an early strike from Camilo Durán helped restore a semblance of calm for the Hoops.

The champions had control of proceedings thereafter and – despite an inspired display from the home goalkeeper Alex Paulsen – Celtic added to their lead through Benjamin Nygren in the 58th minute as they made it seven wins in eight league matches this term.

articles.title: Wade scores 100th Prem try as Red Bulls lose to Exeter
articles.summary: Christian Wade becomes just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 loss at Exeter.
body: Christian Wade became just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter.
Wade, 35, went over twice in the first half - his second giving the Red Bulls a two-point half-time lead - before pouncing on a Henry Slade error to race in for a third early in the second half.
Newcastle's former England winger is now just one try off the all-time Prem try record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023.

Wade, who spent four years trying to break into the NFL from 2018, returned to the Prem in 2024 with Gloucester after two years at French side Racing 92, last year moving to Newcastle after a brief spell at rugby league's Wigan Warriors.

articles.title: European football: Lazio join Inter at top of Serie A as Roma held at Como
articles.summary: Gattuso’s side ease to 3-1 win against 10-man Monza. Roma frustrated after goalless draw away at Como. Lazio moved level on points with Inter at the top of Serie A with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday as 10-man Roma played out the first goalless draw of the Italian season at Como.
body: Under Gennaro Gattuso, who has bounced back after his failure at the helm of the Italian national side who missed out on the 2026 World Cup, Lazio continued their strong start to the season. Still unbeaten, the Roman outfit secured a fifth victory in six matches to pull level on 16 points with Inter, who beat Parma 3-0 at San Siro on Saturday.

Nuno Tavares gave Lazio a third-minute lead and Gustav Isaksen doubled it midway through the first half. Monza had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off on 35 minutes for hauling down Tijjani Noslin as he broke through on goal, but the 16th-placed visitors rattled Lazio after the break, pulling a goal back and coming close to equalising before conceding a third goal in the closing stages.

Roma left Como frustrated, having managed only a single point. The dismissal of league top scorer Donyell Malen for a dangerous tackle early in the second half forced them to scale back their ambitions. Neither team could find the breakthrough in a clash between two sides widely regarded as dark horses for the title, leaving Inter and Lazio two points clear of Roma after their respective wins over Parma and Monza.

articles.title: Jaguars and Eagles have two players ejected after opening-kickoff brawl in London
articles.summary: Jaguars’ opening kickoff return TD called back. Two players ejected after midfield confrontation. Chaotic scenes force opening kickoff to be replayed. A 90-yard kickoff return for a touchdown nullified and two players ejected.
body: It was quite a start to the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Jaguars rookie Josh Cameron returned the opening kickoff 90 yards for a would-be touchdown, but it was called back because of offsetting penalties, including a hold by Jacksonville’s Branson Combs.
Meanwhile, there was a scrum at midfield, with pushing and shoving on both sides.
When the dust settled, two players were ejected: Jacksonville’s Bryan Thomas Jr and Philadelphia’s Jeremiah Trotter Jr.

articles.title: Sensational Smith, relentless quicks - Australia veterans serve reminder
articles.summary: The fearsome pace quartet and Steve Smith's brilliance serves as a reminder of Australia's quality as the tourists take charge against South Africa.
body: Viewed by many in England as there for the taking in last winter's Ashes despite a 4-1 win, they are also labelled too old by many observers at home.
The victims of recent shock defeats by West Indies and Bangladesh, they are still unbeaten in their past nine Test series.

But while their struggling batting line-up was bailed out by Matt Renshaw across the first two days of the first Test in Durban, they took control over South Africa on day three in an all-too familiar way.

Nine years after they first appeared together as Australia's bowling quartet, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon produced their latest relentless performance to dismiss South Africa for 284. There was even some magic from Steve Smith thrown in too.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels is back for Commanders in Week 5, but some NFL doctors think this is stupid
articles.summary: Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Washington Commanders will get Jayden Daniels back in Week 5. Washington’s franchise quarterback is finally back from his elbow injury. But some doctors around the NFL are skeptical about his return to the field.
body: Jayden Daniels is back for Commanders in Week 5, but some NFL doctors think this is stupid appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Daniels visited multiple specialists in New York and Los Angeles following his latest elbow injury. The overwhelming opinion was that playing with a brace was a viable option. However, not all doctors are convinced that it is such a good idea.

Multiple doctors around the NFL believe that a player who dislocates his elbow twice is at a higher risk of suffering another dislocation, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. It is important to note that those opinions are coming from doctors who have not examined Daniels personally. Instead, they seem to be sharing general medical opinions.
Daniels has suffered two elbow dislocations on the same arm over the past year.

articles.summary: Wales forward Elise Hughes admits reaching the World Cup would fulfil a lifelong ambition.

articles.title: Milan forced into early change against Sassuolo as Gabbia stretchered off in tears
articles.summary: Milan defender Matteo Gabbia suffered an unfortunate injury just over a quarter of an hour into his side’s Serie A match away against Sassuolo on Sunday evening, forcing Ruben Amorim into an early substitution after being carried off on a stretcher.
body: You can follow the action from all of Sunday’s Serie A matches on the Football Italia Liveblog.

This was Gabbia’s first start of the 2026-27 season, appearing twice off the bench at the beginning of the campaign before suffering a minor ankle issue in September. He was part of a Rossoneri back four that included Mario Gila at right-back, Pervis Estupinan at left-back and Strahinja Pavlovic as his centre-back partner.
His evening lasted for just over 15 minutes, though, after going down hurt while attempting to nick the ball off Armand Lauriente on the touchline on Sassuolo’s left wing.
Gabbia stretched for the ball, but was unable to get back off the deck as the referee waved for play to be continued: No foul had been committed either way.

articles.title: Smith vows 'karma' will get Suljovic after antics at Swiss Darts Trophy
articles.summary: Ross Smith has vowed that "karma" will catch up with opponent Mensur Suljovic after the Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in round three of the Swiss Darts Trophy.
body: The two players were deadlocked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and give his opponent a chance at the match.

Suljovic then nailed a double 10 with his last dart to secure the checkout and the victory, although his unsportsmanlike antics left a sour taste in Smith's mouth, later taking to X to post his thoughts after the defeat.
"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.
"Obviously it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.

articles.title: Verstappen claims dominant first Singapore GP win
articles.summary: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career with a dominant victory, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton endured a messy race strategically to tumble off the podium late on.
body: Verstappen led every lap on his way to a second consecutive win despite being unable to communicate with the team due to a radio problem, but it did not affect him as he held off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who eventually finished seven seconds behind in second.

Kimi Antonelli took advantage of an elbows-out battle late on between Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, with the seven-time world champion on old tyres in the latter stages, to take third and extend his lead over George Russell to 102 points in the Drivers' Championship.
It means Antonelli can become world champion at the next race in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1, should he outscore Russell by 23 points and Hamilton by 14 points.
Russell recovered to ninth in Sunday's race after starting 19th due to grid penalties for a new power unit, as overtaking proved very difficult at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

articles.title: Palace stun Forest on Glasner's Selhurst Park return
articles.summary: Crystal Palace turned Oliver Glasner's Selhurst Park return on its head, coming from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 after a remarkable afternoon in south London.
body: Glasner received warm applause before kick-off in recognition of the trophies he delivered at the club. But, as Palace took control, the mood changed, with chants of 'Glasner, what's the score?' and 'Sacked in the morning!' ringing around the stadium.

Palace owed much to Walter Benitez, who produced a string of superb saves to deny Liam Delap, Morgan Gibbs-White and, later, Chris Wood. His interventions kept the hosts in the contest as Forest dominated early on, before Daichi Kamada's first Premier League goal and Jefferson Lerma's first-half stoppage-time header turned the game around.

Yeremy Pino extended Palace's lead in the 59th minute, reacting quickest after Matz Sels saved Jorgen Strand Larsen's effort. It ended a run of 19 Premier League appearances without a goal for the Spaniard and capped a remarkable shift in momentum, with Palace looking increasingly dangerous after the break.
